marks.gloss_en: what is the reason? damage that is not noticeable is not damage; [it is] a rabbinic fine -- him the Rabbis penalized, his son they did not
the mishna: a firstborn was pursuing him, he kicked it and made a blemish in it -- one may slaughter it on that [blemish]
Rav Pappa: they taught this only where he kicked it at the time of the pursuit
version 2, Rav Pappa: do not say at the time of the pursuit yes and not at the time no -- rather even after the pursuit too [one may slaughter on it]
Rav Yehuda: it is permitted to make a blemish in a firstborn before it has come out into the air of the world
Rava: [where] it eats and it is not seen, it opens [its mouth wide] and it is seen -- it is a blemish
the quaestor took a dagger and slit its ear; the incident came before the Sages and they permitted it
children playing in the field tied lambs' tails together, and the tail of one, a firstborn, was severed; the Sages permitted it
reading 1: the mishna's 'Israelite shepherds' are [Israelites] in the house of priests -- they are believed
reading 1: 'priest shepherds' are priests in the house of an Israelite -- they are not believed
a priest [testifying] for a priest is likewise not believed (reading 1: 'the same holds'; reading 2: 'all the more so')
and RSbG comes to say: he is believed about his fellow's, and not believed about his own
reading 2: the mishna's 'Israelite shepherds' [of an Israelite] who are priests -- they are believed
R' Meir (the mishna): one suspect regarding a matter may neither judge it nor testify about it
מכדי ממילא הוא, מה לי היה מה לי נעשה -- both phrasings mean it happens by itself
Rava: rather, 'was made' too [means] by itself, and there is no difference
it is necessary: had it taught us [only] the gentile -- [permitted] since he will not come to make a habit of it; but a minor, who will come to make a habit of it -- say not
and had it taught us [only] the minor -- since he will not be confused with an adult; but a gentile, who will be confused with an adult -- say not. [So] it is necessary
Rav Ketina: they taught [it is permitted] only where they said to him 'unless it had a blemish'; but if they said 'if a blemish was made in it', it is as if they told him 'go make a blemish in it'
'any that is with intent is forbidden' -- to include what? to include grama [indirect causation]
'not with intent' -- to include one who speaks offhandedly
